meta.title: The Bird House Opens
meta.textType: functional: a short TV news report, with a map

paragraphs: On Friday, March twelfth, at six o'clock, the evening news came on. Lily and Tom sat on the sofa in the living room, and Dad sat in an armchair. Pip sat on the floor and looked at the screen. The first story was about the small zoo. A reporter stood in front of a new glass house, and the headline said "THE BIRD HOUSE OPENS." "Good evening," said the reporter. "I am at the small zoo, and this is a big event for our town." Lily looked at Tom and said, "That is where the Explorers are going tomorrow!"

"Here is a map of the town," said the reporter. She pointed at the key. "It shows the zoo, the bus station, the bridge, the library, and the post office." "Tourists and local families can take a bus from the bus station to the zoo." "The bird house opens to visitors tomorrow, and it is open from nine o'clock to five o'clock," she said. "Children under fourteen come in free." "I am thirteen, so is it free for me?" asked Tom. "Yes, you are under fourteen, so it is free," said Dad. "Then let's go on Sunday!" said Tom. "We may go if the weather is good," said Dad.

Next, the screen showed the inside of the bird house. A green parrot sat on a branch behind the glass. Pip stood up and barked at it. Lily and Tom laughed. "He thinks that the parrot is a visitor," said Dad. The clock on the wall showed five past six. "Many of these birds were wild birds before they came here," said the reporter. "Now they have a warm, safe home."

The reporter walked to the zoo gate. "It was painted last week, and modern glass windows have just been fitted," she said. A local painter put twenty animals on the gate. "Can you find all of them?" she asked. Then she stood next to a little green train. It broke down two years ago, but it was fixed last month. She held up an old paper. "This is the zoo's first animal list," she said. "This document was found in a box last week."

"The old bridge next to the zoo was built a century ago," said the reporter. "From the bridge, visitors have a good view of the pond." "A bird house, a train, and an old list!" said Tom. "The Explorers take the bus from the school gate at half past eight," said Lily. "Will Pip go too?" asked Dad. "No, Pip stays at home," said Lily.

Pip put his head on Dad's foot and closed his eyes. The reporter smiled at the camera. "Come and see the birds tomorrow," she said. That was the news from the small zoo. "See you tomorrow, parrot!" whispered Lily.
text.summary: Lily, Tom, and Dad watch a TV news report about the new bird house at the small zoo. The report tells what is new, shows a map of the town, and says when the zoo is open.
